note: Live OakGuard run: muse-wonder-1.0 proposed rules for 3 escapes, graded by the referee at record time. Replays re-grade this text with the current referee.

exchanges.content: {"description": "Flags any length builtin called with a numeric literal length that is not a positive integer, such as 0, a negative number, or a fractional number, which produces no finite output.", "family": "positive-int-length", "fixHint": "Replace the flagged length argument with a positive integer >= 1, e.g. change sma(close, 0) to sma(close, 14), or use a variable guaranteed to hold a positive integer; never use 0, negative, or fractional lengths.", "issueCode": "NON_POSITIVE_INTEGER_LENGTH", "name": "Length arguments must be positive integers", "params": {"allowObjectMethods": false, "followVariables": false, "functions": [], "operators": [], "windowFunctions": []}, "rationale": "The seed uses sma(close, 0); a zero, negative, or fractional literal length is invalid for every length builtin and yields no finite values, while legitimate scripts use positive integer literals or variables."}

{
  "description": "Flags unknown dotted builtin calls such as array.avgg that silently return 0",
  "family": "unknown-dotted-call",
  "fixHint": "Replace the unknown dotted call with a registered builtin with the correct spelling, e.g. change array.avgg(vals) to array.avg(vals). Check the namespace and method name against the builtin registry (array.*, math.*, line.*, table.*, color.*, etc.) and do not use invented or misspelled method names.",
  "issueCode": "UNKNOWN_DOTTED_CALL",
  "name": "Unknown dotted builtin call",
  "params": {
    "allowObjectMethods": true,
    "followVariables": false,
    "functions": [],
    "operators": [],
    "windowFunctions": []
  }
  ,
  "rationale": "array.avgg is not a registered builtin; the correct name is array.avg. Allowing known runtime object methods (push, get, set, sum, avg, size, etc.) avoids flagging legitimate OakRing/Matrix/table handle methods while still flagging misspelled names like avgg on any object or namespace."
}

{"description": "Flags a comparison between a price series (open, high, low, close) and a highest()/lowest() window over a price series evaluated on the same bar, with no [k] history offset on the window.", "family": "self-inclusive-window", "fixHint": "Offset the channel window by one bar so it excludes the current bar: use highest(high, len)[1] and lowest(low, len)[1] (e.g. upper = highest(high, len)[1], lower = lowest(low, len)[1]) before comparing or crossing close against them.", "issueCode": "SELF_INCLUSIVE_WINDOW_BREAKOUT", "name": "Self-inclusive breakout window", "params": {"allowObjectMethods": false, "followVariables": true, "functions": [], "operators": [">", "<", "crossover", "crossunder"], "windowFunctions": []}, "rationale": "close can never exceed highest(high) or fall below lowest(low) when the current bar is included in the window, so breakouts never fire; offsetting the window by [1] compares against prior bars only."}
